6º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Past simple: regular and irregular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about finished actions in the past (acciones terminadas)
  • Add -ed to regular verbs with the right spelling
  • Learn the most common irregular verbs
  • Make negatives and questions with did / didn't
  • Talk about past habits with used to
  • Learn a bigger list of irregular verbs
  • Make subject questions without did
  • Use the past continuous with the past simple to tell stories

Para pensar

En español decimos «ayer jugué» y «ayer fui». En inglés, «jugué» es played, pero «fui» no es «goed». ¿Por qué?

Explicación

1. What is the past simple?

We use the past simple for actions that started and finished in the past: «I visited my cousins last summer», «We watched a film yesterday». We often say when it happened.

En castellano: equivale a nuestro pretérito: «visité», «vimos». Una gran ventaja del inglés: el verbo no cambia según la persona. «I played», «you played», «he played», «they played». ¡No hay que memorizar seis terminaciones como en español!

2. Used to: past habits

We use used to + verb to talk about habits or situations that were true in the past but are not true now:

  • «I used to sleep with a teddy bear.» (Antes dormía con un osito; ahora no.)
  • «My grandma used to live in a village.» (Ahora vive en la ciudad.)
  • «There used to be a cinema in my street.»

Negatives and questions use did, and then use to without -d:

  • «I didn't use to like vegetables.» (Antes no me gustaban.)
  • «Did you use to watch cartoons?» – «Yes, I did.»

En castellano: used to equivale muchas veces a nuestro pretérito imperfecto (jugaba, vivía) o a «solía»: «I used to play in the park» = «Jugaba / Solía jugar en el parque».

Careful: the past simple tells us about one finished action («Yesterday I played in the park»), but used to tells us about something we did many times in the past.

Try it! Think about when you were five years old. What did you use to eat for breakfast? What toys did you use to play with? Where did you use to go on holiday? Ask a partner and compare your answers: «I used to love dinosaurs. Did you use to love them too?»

3. Regular verbs: -ed

Regular verbs add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, watch → watched, help → helped.

Spelling rules: verbs ending in -e add only -d: like → liked, dance → danced. Consonant + y changes to -ied: study → studied, cry → cried (but play → played, because a vowel comes before the y). Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped, plan → planned.

4. How do you say -ed?

The ending -ed has three sounds. After most sounds it is /d/: played, cleaned, opened. After sounds like p, k, s, sh, ch it is /t/: walked («wokt»), watched («wocht»), helped («helpt»).

After t or d it is a new syllable /ɪd/: wanted («uóntid»), needed («nídid»), visited. En castellano: casi nunca se pronuncia «-ed» completo; solo cuando el verbo acaba en t o d. Di en voz alta: «I walked to the park and I wanted an ice cream».

5. Irregular verbs

Many common verbs are irregular: they don't add -ed. You need to learn them by heart (de memoria). Here are some of the most useful: go → went, have → had, eat → ate, see → saw, buy → bought, get → got, make → made, come → came, take → took, write → wrote, swim → swam, run → ran.

The verb to be has two forms: was (I, he, she, it) and were (you, we, they). «It was sunny», «We were at the beach».

6. More irregular verbs

Here is a list of more irregular verbs that you will use a lot. Read them aloud in groups of five and test yourself every day:

  • be → was / were · become → became · begin → began · break → broke · bring → brought
  • catch → caught · choose → chose · drink → drank · drive → drove · fall → fell
  • feel → felt · find → found · fly → flew · forget → forgot · give → gave
  • know → knew · leave → left · lose → lost · meet → met · ride → rode
  • run → ran · sleep → slept · speak → spoke · take → took · tell → told
  • wear → wore · win → won · throw → threw · understand → understood · stand → stood

Tips: make flashcards with the verb on one side and the past on the other; write a funny sentence with each one («I forgot my shoes and lost my hat!»); or sing them with a rhythm. Many verbs follow patterns: know → knew, throw → threw, fly → flew; sleep → slept, feel → felt, leave → left, meet → met.

7. Tricks to learn irregular verbs

Group them by sound and it's easier (agrúpalos por cómo suenan). -ought / -aught: buy → bought, bring → brought, think → thought, teach → taught. i → a: swim → swam, sing → sang, drink → drank, begin → began. Same form: put → put, cut → cut, hit → hit.

Make flashcards (tarjetas): the verb on one side, the past on the other. Practise five verbs a day. Sing them with a rhythm: «go, went – see, saw – eat, ate!». En castellano: no intentes aprender cien de golpe; los veinte más usados ya cubren casi todo.

8. Negatives with didn't

To make a negative we use didn't (did not) + the verb in its normal form: «I didn't play football yesterday», «She didn't go to school». Careful: after didn't we never use the past: not «didn't went».

The verb to be is different: it doesn't need didn't. We say «I wasn't tired», «They weren't at home». En castellano: did ya lleva el pasado; por eso el verbo vuelve a su forma básica, igual que en el presente con doesn't.

9. Questions with did

For questions we put Did at the beginning and the verb in its normal form: «Did you enjoy the trip?» – «Yes, I did. / No, I didn't». «Did he see the dolphins?» – «Yes, he did».

With question words: «Where did you go?», «What did you eat?», «When did they arrive?». With to be: «Was it fun?», «Were you scared?». Time words for the past: yesterday, last night, last week, last summer, two days ago, in 2024.

10. Who broke the window?

Usually, past questions need did: «What did you eat?», «Where did she go?». But there is an important exception!

When the question word (who or what) is the subject of the sentence, that is, when we ask who did the action, we don't use did, and the verb stays in the past:

  • «Who broke the window?» – «Tom did.» (not «Who did break…?»)
  • «Who ate my sandwich?» – «The dog did!»
  • «What happened?» – «There was an accident.»
  • «Who won the match?» – «Spain won.»

Compare these two questions:

  • «Who did you see at the party?» – «I saw Ana.» (you is the subject; we ask about the object.)
  • «Who saw you at the party?» – «Ana saw me.» (who is the subject.)

En castellano no tenemos este problema, porque no usamos un auxiliar como did: «¿Quién rompió la ventana?» y «¿A quién viste?».

11. Reading: my best holiday

Read Hugo's text: «Last summer I went to Asturias with my family. We stayed in a small house near the sea. On the first day it rained, so we visited a museum. Then the sun came out and we swam every day. I tried cheese from the mountains – it was delicious! We didn't take many photos, but I wrote a diary. It was the best holiday ever.»

Find six regular verbs and six irregular ones. Which verbs are in the negative?

12. Let's practise: guess my weekend

Play in groups. Write three sentences about last weekend: two true and one false (una falsa). «I went to the cinema. I ate sushi. I played tennis». Your classmates ask questions to find the false one: «Did you go with your family?», «What film did you see?».

Then write a short text about a special day. Use time order words: first, then, after that, finally. Consejo: repasa al final si cada verbo está en pasado y si después de did has usado la forma normal.

13. Past continuous: what were you doing?

To tell stories we often need another past tense: the past continuous. We form it with was / were + verb-ing:

  • «I was reading a comic.» · «They were playing football.»
  • Negative: «She wasn't sleeping.» · Question: «What were you doing?»

We use it for an action that was in progress at a moment in the past: «At eight o'clock last night I was having dinner.»

It is very useful together with the past simple. The past continuous is the long background action, and the past simple is the short action that interrupts it. We join them with when or while:

  • «I was having a shower when the phone rang.»
  • «While we were walking in the forest, we saw a deer.»
  • «It was raining when we arrived.»

En castellano se parece a «estaba + gerundio»: «Estaba duchándome cuando sonó el teléfono».

14. Famous firsts

History is full of «firsts». Read these sentences and look at the past simple verbs:

  • In 1903, the Wright brothers flew the first powered plane in the USA. The first flight lasted only 12 seconds!
  • In 1928, Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, by accident: some mould grew in one of his dishes.
  • In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the top of Mount Everest for the first time.
  • In 1963, Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space.
  • On 20th July 1969, Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon. He said: «That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.»
  • In 1903, Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize. She was the first woman to win it, and later she won a second one.

Spain has some famous firsts too. In 1888, Isaac Peral launched one of the first electric submarines in the world. In 1906, Santiago Ramón y Cajal became the first Spanish scientist to win a Nobel Prize, for his discoveries about the nerve cells of the brain. And in 1923, Juan de la Cierva flew his autogiro, an aircraft with a rotor on top, the grandfather of the modern helicopter. All of them worked for years, made many mistakes and tried again and again before they succeeded.

Now it's your turn: find out about a «first» in your town or your family and write three sentences about it in the past simple. When did it happen? Who did it? What happened next?

Past simple

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: play, like, cry, plan.

  2. Write the past: go, eat, see, buy.

  3. Complete with was or were: «The film ___ great. We ___ happy.»

  4. Make it negative: «He wrote a letter.»

  5. Make a question: «You had lunch at school.»

  6. How do you pronounce -ed in «wanted», «watched», «played»?

  7. Correct: «Yesterday I swimmed in the pool.»

  8. Answer: «Did you watch TV last night?» (no)

  9. Translate: «La semana pasada visitamos a mi abuela.»

  10. Write three sentences about your last birthday.

  11. Write the past: catch, drink, fly, win.

  12. Complete: «I ___ to have long hair.» (used)

  13. What year did Neil Armstrong walk on the Moon?

  14. Choose: «Who (ate / did eat) my cake?»

  15. Complete: «They ___ (play) football at five o'clock.»

  16. Write two things you used to do when you were little.

  17. Make a question with did: «You met Ana at the park.»

  18. Make a subject question: «Mario won the race.»

  19. Join with when: «I was walking home. It started to rain.»

  20. Who was Valentina Tereshkova?

  21. Write a negative and a question with used to.

  22. Explain the difference between «I played tennis yesterday» and «I used to play tennis».

  23. Write a short story (5 sentences) with two past continuous and three past simple verbs.

  24. Interview an older person about their childhood and write five sentences with used to.

Practica

  1. The past of «walk» is…

    1. A) walkt
    2. B) walked
    3. C) walk

  2. The past of «go» is…

    1. A) goed
    2. B) gone
    3. C) went

  3. The past of «study» is…

    1. A) studied
    2. B) studyed
    3. C) studed

  4. «___ you enjoy the party?»

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Were
    3. C) Did

  5. «She didn't ___ the bus.»

    1. A) took
    2. B) take
    3. C) takes

  6. «They ___ at the beach yesterday.»

    1. A) were
    2. B) was
    3. C) did

  7. The past of «eat» is…

    1. A) eated
    2. B) ate
    3. C) eaten

  8. Which is a past time expression?

    1. A) every day
    2. B) now
    3. C) two days ago

  9. The past of «stop» is…

    1. A) stopped
    2. B) stoped
    3. C) stopt

  10. In «wanted», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

  11. «I ___ use to like broccoli.»

    1. A) don't
    2. B) didn't
    3. C) wasn't

  12. The past of «leave» is…

    1. A) leaved
    2. B) leaft
    3. C) left

  13. «What ___?» – «There was an accident.»

    1. A) did happen
    2. B) happened
    3. C) happens

  14. «While we ___ dinner, the lights went out.»

    1. A) were having
    2. B) had
    3. C) are having

  15. The first woman to win a Nobel Prize was…

    1. A) Valentina Tereshkova
    2. B) Anne Frank
    3. C) Marie Curie

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el pasado simple; Cómo se forma el pasado de los verbos regulares y su ortografía; Qué son los verbos irregulares y algunos ejemplos; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas con did.

Resumen

Glosario

Used to
Expresión para hábitos pasados (solía).
Habit
Hábito, algo que se hace a menudo.
Irregular verb
Verbo que no forma el pasado con -ed.
Subject
Sujeto: quien hace la acción.
Subject question
Pregunta sobre quién hace la acción, sin did.
Past continuous
Pasado continuo: was/were + -ing.
Interrupt
Interrumpir.
While
Mientras.
Powered plane
Avión con motor.
Mould
Moho.
Reach
Llegar a, alcanzar.
Mankind
La humanidad.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Past simpleAcciones terminadas en el pasado.
-edPasado regular: walked, played.
-ied / doble consonantestudied · stopped.
go → wentIrregular muy frecuente.
was / werePasado de to be.
didn't + verboNegativa: I didn't go.
Did…?Pregunta: Did you see it?
agoHace: two days ago = hace dos días.
Used toPast habits: I used to play… / I didn't use to… / Did you use to…?
More irregularscaught, chose, felt, knew, left, slept, took, wore, won.
Subject questionsWho broke…? What happened? – no did.
Past continuouswas/were + -ing; long action interrupted by past simple (when/while).

Soluciones

  1. B) Regular: + -ed.
  2. C) Irregular.
  3. A) Consonante + y → -ied.
  4. C) Pregunta en pasado: Did.
  5. B) Tras didn't, forma normal.
  6. A) They + were.
  7. B) Irregular.
  8. C) Ago = hace.
  9. A) Se dobla la p.
  10. B) Tras t o d, sílaba nueva.
  11. B) Negative of used to.
  12. C) Irregular.
  13. B) Subject question.
  14. A) Past continuous.
  15. C) 1903.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. played, liked, cried, planned.
  2. went, ate, saw, bought.
  3. was, were.
  4. He didn't write a letter.
  5. Did you have lunch at school?
  6. /ɪd/, /t/, /d/.
  7. Yesterday I swam in the pool.
  8. No, I didn't.
  9. Last week we visited my grandma.
  10. Model answer: I had a party. My friends came to my house. We ate a chocolate cake.
  11. caught, drank, flew, won.
  12. used.
  13. In 1969.
  14. ate.
  15. were playing.
  16. Open answer. Example: I used to sleep with a teddy bear.
  17. Who did you meet at the park?
  18. Who won the race?
  19. I was walking home when it started to rain.
  20. The first woman in space (1963).
  21. Open answer. Example: I didn't use to like fish. Did you use to play with dolls?
  22. The first is one finished action; the second is a past habit that is not true now.
  23. Open answer.
  24. Open answer.
